answer: For every observation the night astronomer opens the dome shutter and signs the log with the object, the hour and the seeing, and the log is kept for the observatory's life. A pearl observation claimed without opening the dome fails the log: at the sparrow of the shutter the stars must have been visible on the night claimed, and a false claim shows a cloudy sky. Forging the log means keeping the dome for two years, signing 500 nights and paying 17,300, while the orchard signature in the shutter log is read by the director each month, so an observation whose shutter never opened is erased.
